summary: wc counts, sort orders lines, and uniq removes repeated lines. Together they answer questions like "how many different names?" and "who scored highest?"
notes: wc notes.txt prints 3 numbers before the name: lines, words, and bytes.
In sort -t, -k3 -n -r, -t, splits on commas, -k3 sorts by the 3rd column, -n compares as numbers, and -r reverses so the highest is first.
tail -n +2 starts at line 2, which skips the header row name,grade,score. cut -d, -f2 keeps only the 2nd column.
pitfall: uniq without sort misses duplicates that are not next to each other. uniq cs/roster.txt still has 10 lines because the second Ava and Leo are at the end. Use sort | uniq.
